question: Can a GitHub issue/comment/event identity provide a zero-cost Chat-visible witness outside rewindable Git ref state that survives or fail-closes deletion/recreation/editability rollback strongly enough to close same-repository force-ref ABA?

connected_capability_observation.event_surface: No first-class connected mutation action for issue events was exposed in the inspected GitHub connector; public REST GET/list issue-event endpoints remain readable through lightweight repository transport.
connected_capability_observation.reason_no_live_mutation: Role-authorized evidence/checkpoint work did not require user-visible issue lifecycle mutation; this leaf tested capability and platform semantics only.

public_sources.title: REST API endpoints for issue events - GitHub Docs
public_sources.observed_semantics: The current REST surface exposes list/get issue-event endpoints, with each event carrying id, Global Node ID and created_at. The issue-scoped list endpoint documents 410 Gone. No create/update/delete issue-event endpoint is listed.

public_sources.title: Issue event types - GitHub Docs
public_sources.observed_semantics: Issue-event objects document id as the unique identifier of the event and node_id as the Global Node ID of the event.

public_sources.title: REST API endpoints for issues - GitHub Docs
public_sources.observed_semantics: Fetching a deleted issue can return 410 Gone to an authenticated reader with access; transferred issues can return 301.

public_sources.title: Deleting an issue - GitHub Docs
public_sources.observed_semantics: Repository administrators/owners can permanently delete issues under documented permission conditions.

public_sources.title: Editing an issue - GitHub Docs
public_sources.observed_semantics: Issue title/body are editable, and issue-description edit history can itself be removed by authorized users.

public_sources.title: REST API endpoints for issue comments - GitHub Docs
public_sources.observed_semantics: Issue comments have explicit update and delete endpoints, so comment content/history is not append-only.

same_repository_force_ref_rewind.reason: Git ref movement does not itself mutate the issue-event service. A pinned event object would therefore not be rolled back by a branch force-update.

issue_body_or_comment_as_witness.reason: Issue body/title and comments are editable; comments are deletable; issue-description edit history can be removed.

issue_event_object_as_immutable_record.reason: The public issue-event REST surface is read-only (list/get) and event objects have unique ids/node_ids, which is favorable for tamper evidence. However the event is owned by an issue lifecycle that can be permanently deleted.

delete_issue_then_recreate_activity.reason: Deletion is externally observable as Gone when access permits, so a verifier that rejects missing witness state can fail closed. But the reviewed public docs do not state a no-reuse theorem for issue numbers/event ids/node_ids after deletion/recreation, so restoration of an indistinguishable prior witness is not formally excluded by this leaf.

monotonic_latest_event_selection.reason: The reviewed issue-event list documentation does not specify a repository-wide monotonic event counter or list ordering guarantee. A unique event id is an object identity, not by itself a monotonic counter.

dedicated_append_per_protected_state_tra.reason: Issue events are generated by issue/pull-request activity; there is no direct create-issue-event endpoint. Producing a witness event would require an auxiliary issue mutation such as a label/state/milestone operation.

bottom_line: Issue-event identity is meaningfully better than issue/comment content because it lives outside Git ref state and the public event API is read-only. It can be a fail-closed tamper sentinel when a pinned event disappears. It does not yet close same-repository force-ref ABA: this leaf found no documented monotonic allocator/order guarantee, no documented id non-reuse guarantee across deletion/recreation, and no direct append-event primitive. Do not promote it as the required non-rewindable monotonic witness.
tested_scope: Connected GitHub capability schemas plus official current GitHub issue/event/comment documentation. No issue creation/edit/delete, no event-producing mutation, no branch/ref mutation, no protected-primary authority, no manual execution, no hosted compute, no optional monthly/trial/paid quota, no multi-object atomicity test and no network-partition test.
continuation: Test exactly one adjacent zero-cost candidate next: whether GitHub's repository-scoped issue/PR number allocator has an official monotonic/no-reuse property across issue deletion and recreation strong enough to provide an externally queryable counter. Reject absent an explicit guarantee; do not start another witness family in the same invocation.
